deepdive.sec: Housing Finance — low-income / affordable HFC (Tier-3/Tier-4 "emerging" branch-led)

bull_bear.body:
- **Tier 1 at 42.9% + Tier 2 0.5%** — an analyst (Karan Gupta, CAVI Capital) directly challenged this as "dragging down our ROE significantly."
- **No buyback / capital return:** "I think there's no current plan of handing it back to shareholders as of now. We believe we will require capital for growth, and that was the intention of raising **INR1,000 crores of primary in IPO** so that at least for the **next 3, 4 years**, we are secured for our growth plans."
- Defence of the buffer: "40% to 43% capital adequacy, if you see most of the peer sets… most of the peer group of companies who are doing affordable finance is sitting on similar levels… The overall risk weight of the balance sheet comes at about **45%**… in case in future, there is any changes in the risk weights, this can impact our capital adequacy." Plus "about **6% to 7% of capital that we set aside for operating risk** as per best practice ICAAP methodology."
- Implication: ROE stays structurally below ROA-implied potential until leverage builds — management's own path is 14.7% now → "around 17% ROE" a couple of years out.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **The 45–50 branch target vs 7 actual adds in two quarters** — the single most checkable FY27 commitment.
2. **Q2 must deliver the catch-up.** "close to 25% or upward of 23%, 24%" disbursement growth; if Q2 does not absorb the Q1 carry-forward, the 17–18% full-year disbursement guide is at risk.
3. **Rates turning.** Management explicitly flags "a general view that the interest rates may go up" and hedges with repricing — but its own policy is *not* to pass through 1–2 month moves, so a short sharp rise compresses spread before any pass-through.
4. **West Asia / geopolitics** — "the ongoing geopolitical uncertainty around the West Asia situation and its resulting impact on segments like fuel-dependent trade and travel." Already caused self-imposed restrictions in export-oriented branches and the non-home-loan slowdown.
5. **Monsoon** — "the monsoon outlook given it's bearing on the rural and semi-urban cash flows" (its core geography).
6. **Competitive intensity from new entrants** into affordable housing — mitigated, per management, by being "1 notch below."
7. **ROE drag from 43% capital adequacy** with no return-of-capital plan.
8. **Recognition-change comparability** — FY27 quarters are not like-for-like with FY26 on disbursement; two basis changes in three years (Q1FY25 handover, Q1FY27 realisation).
9. **State-level softness (MP, Telangana)** management could not explain on the call.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident and specific; MD pushed back on the framing of a bad quarter — "maybe on a lighter note, 1 correction that it was not a challenging quarter. I think the quarter was good, while we took a conscious call of looking at disbursement on clearance, I think it was a well-informed call. And I would say it was slightly delayed because of the systemic changes that we were wanting to do."
- Framed the recognition change as governance-first: "a forward-looking approach and a significant milestone in our commitment to governance, transparency and putting customer at the forefront" — and positioned it as catch-up rather than leadership: "most of the companies have already moved to cheque realization. I think in the true spirit of RBI circular, this was warranted. And we took a little more time because of systemic changes."
- Willing to say "I don't know" — on the MP/Telangana AUM-per-branch question ("unfortunately, readily, I don't have the data") and on the prior-quarter cost of funds ("Last quarter number, I wouldn't have it exactly now. I'll try to pull it during the call").
- Guidance reaffirmed by both MD (opening) and CFO (closing) — unusually explicit double commitment.
- No hedging on capital return: a flat "no" rather than a deferral.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
1. **The disbursement "miss" is definitionally recoverable.** Unlike a demand miss, the cheque-realisation gap is a 5–7 day timing wedge; the deferred volume mechanically lands in Q2, which is why management can put a 23–25% number on Q2 with unusual specificity.
2. **Yield is being defended by geography, not pricing.** Delhi (a low-yield state) grew its contribution and yields still held — the 450+/628 emerging-branch mix, not any pricing action, is doing the work. Ticket size range-bound at INR 11L "while in the market, we see the ticket size has substantially jumped for a lot of players" is the cleanest evidence Aadhar has NOT drifted up-market to chase volume.
3. **Q1 credit-cost seasonality was *better* than its own history** — the seasonal Stage-move is "anywhere between 30 bps to 35 bps. In our case, now it has gone up by 25 bps" — a detail buried under a headline GNPA that merely looks flat.
4. **NHB is a genuine funding arbitrage.** Fresh NHB at 6.9% (with an AHF slice at 4.3%) against ex-NHB incremental of 7.4–7.5% and an overall incremental of 7.3% — 24% of borrowings sourced structurally below market is a durable spread contributor for low-income HFCs specifically.
5. **The AI disclosure is unusually concrete for an affordable HFC** (6 layers, 5 platforms, each tiered to NPA / TAT / cost-to-income / retention / yield) and is being explicitly underwritten as future cost-to-assets benefit *over and above* the guided 6–7 bps/year — i.e. it is optionality not yet in guidance.
6. **Capital adequacy is a deliberate risk-weight hedge, not laziness** — "the overall risk weight of the balance sheet comes at about 45%… in case in future, there is any changes in the risk weights, this can impact our capital adequacy." The buffer is being held against a *regulatory* scenario, which reframes the ROE debate.
7. **Retention is a moat with a P&L price.** The retention team has "delegation on what are the yields they can drop for a consumer" — i.e. the 5% BT-out rate is partly bought with yield concessions, so BT-out and incremental yield must be read together.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capitalisation is equity-heavy: Capital Adequacy Ratio Tier I 42.9% and Tier II 0.5% as on June 30, 2026 (42.0% / 0.5% as on March 31, 2026), with net worth of INR 79 bn.
- Funding base deliberately diversified — "Increasing focus on diversifying borrowings" — with the mix moving from Banks 60% / NHB 22% / NCD 17% / Others 1% at Mar-22 to Banks 49% / NHB 24% / NCD 17% / ECB 7% / Others 3% at Jun-26, across "43 Borrowings Relationships".
- "Positive ALM Position Across Buckets" as of Jun-26 (INR bn): Assets vs Liabilities of 103/72 upto 1 year, 209/176 upto 3 years, 289/235 upto 5 years and 395/363 total, with stated gaps of 32, 32, 54 and 32.
- Rate-reset symmetry disclosed: "73% of Gross AUM and 78% of borrowings have floating interest rates"; incremental borrowing cost (weighted average on fresh borrowings) was 7.3% in Q1 FY27 versus 8.1% in Q1 FY26 and 7.8% in FY26.
- Balance sheet at June 30, 2026 (INR Mn): Share capital 4,373, Reserves and surplus 74,155, Borrowings 200,093, total 286,312, against Loan Assets 255,170.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Mix:** home loans **73%** of AUM, non-home **27%**; salaried **55%** of AUM; average ticket **INR 11 lakhs** (up from INR 10.4 lakhs); LTV **60%**.
- **Non-home loan slowdown was deliberate:** "a slight reduction in the quarter — in the last 2 quarters… was a part of the design, given the situation around West Asia crisis and by philosophy, non-housing loans being slightly more riskier. I would say it was a conscious decision." Incremental mix is 76-24 vs a historical 70-30.
- **Urban vs emerging is the core operating axis:** "out of the 628 branches, approximately **450 branches plus** happen to be in the emerging locations. Emerging gives me substantially high yields compared to urban locations." Illustrative yields: **urban 11.5–12%, emerging 14–14.8%**; the medium-term target mix is "even if… I reach 50-50."
- **Geography discipline:** "no state contributing on AUM, incremental disbursement and distribution greater than **15%**, that we've been following for the last 5 to 7 years." Delhi (a lower-yield state) rose slightly this quarter with yields still held.
- **State soft spots (analyst-raised):** AUM per branch declined ~3% YoY in Madhya Pradesh and grew only 5–6% in Telangana; management did not have the data on the call — "there will be certain branches where we put restrictions, certain states where we put restrictions in terms of which were more export oriented."
- **Liability book:** banks 49% / NHB 24% / NCD 17% / ECB 7% / others 3%. NHB is the cheap leg — fresh NHB at 6.9%, including an AHF tranche at 4.3%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Retention machine (BT-out at 5%, a multi-year build).** "our central retention team of about **20 member teams**. So, every consumer who is desirous of moving out to a different company has to go through the retention team. The retention team is completely equipped with a lot of data analytics inputs in terms of segregating the customers into red amber green… These efforts started or the initiative started about **2 years back**, and it's taken a lot of efforts for us to reach the 5% mark." Result: BT out 5%, "one of the lowest BT out rates in the last 8 to 10 quarters."
- **Segment positioning one notch below the competitive zone.** On new entrants: "They are primarily, as we read the industry, they're coming in the **affordable segment, we are 1 notch below in the low-income segment**. Will there be an overlap between what others do and what we do? Yes, there will be definitely a 5%, 6%, 7% overlap."
- **Distribution depth as the yield moat.** "that strategy of our distribution being large enough, we being in **Tier 3, Tier 4 locations substantially**, and the urban emerging is playing out for us" — evidenced by ticket size staying range-bound (INR 10.4L → INR 11L) "while in the market, we see the ticket size has substantially jumped for a lot of players."
- **Geographic concentration cap** (no state >15% of AUM / incremental disbursement / distribution, held 5–7 years) — cited as the reason West Asia / NRI exposure is a non-event: "our exposure in those states are very low."
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- "HFC focused on low-income housing segment with ticket size less than INR1.5mn, with an AUM of INR314bn", with a "100% secured retail loan book" and a "Granular portfolio skewed towards Salaried customers; Average ticket size of INR1.1mn".
- Value proposition slide lists eight planks: focus on low-income housing; diversified and granular portfolio; extensive branch and sales office network; robust, analytics-driven underwriting and collections; access to diversified funding sources with positive ALM; scalable technology platform; social objectives as a core component of the business model; and an experienced, cycle-tested management team.
- Promoter is Blackstone (through BCP Asia II Holdco VII Pte. Limited), described as "a leading investment firm, with total AUM of US$1.3 trillion" as of June 30, 2026; four of the named directors are Blackstone nominees.
- Deck describes AI as "the operating backbone of AHFL, not a set of projects", institutionalised as an enterprise intelligence layer across origination, underwriting, surveillance, collections and retention, on a stated 6-layer architecture (Data Foundation; Intelligence & Decisioning; Surveillance & Early Warning; Service & Execution; Orchestration; Governance & Trust).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Disbursement basis change] "The Company has transitioned disbursement reporting from cheque handover to cheque realisation basis from Q1 FY 27. Disbursement on cheque handover in Q1 FY 27 is INR 23,590 Mn growth of 19% on YOY basis" — so the reported INR 20,358 Mn and the 23,590 Mn figure are on different bases and are not comparable.
- [Labour code] The 4.4% RoA cited on the introduction slide is marked "*Excluding impact of new labour code arising out of past service cost of Rs.159 Mn (Net of tax Rs.124 Mn)"; the Q1 FY27 highlights slide separately shows ROA of 4.0%.
- [Ratings] Key highlights state "AA+ / Stable CARE rating"; the ratings slide lists Care Ratings, India Ratings and ICRA with values AA / Stable, AA / Positive, AA+ / Stable and A1+ under headings "Old ratings" and "Updated ratings", but the agency-to-rating and old-versus-updated binding is lost in the text extraction and is not asserted here.
- [Ownership history] Pre-merger Aadhar Housing Finance Private Limited was merged into the Company in 2017 under an NCLT-approved scheme (Bengaluru Bench, order dated October 27, 2017) following the merger of DHFL Vysya Housing Finance Limited; the Company was "Acquired by the Blackstone Group in June 2019" and listed in H1 FY25.
- [Regulatory NPA classification] GNPA to AUM of 1.16% for FY23 and 1.46% for Q1 FY24 carry the footnote "Includes 0.04% NPA <= 90 DPD which have been classified as per the RBI circular dated 12th November 2021".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- **Spread held at 5.8%** through a 15 bps RPLR cut effective February 2026. Stated philosophy: "our approach, as always, has been to **protect spreads rather than chase yields**… so that operating leverage does the work that pricing cannot."
- **Incremental yields flat** — "incremental yields, as you would have seen, have remained flat. And I don't see any reason why the incremental yield should drop at any stage."
- **Cost of funds:** exit 7.7% vs 8.0% YoY; "First quarter has been where we have seen very limited movement in cost of funds." Risk acknowledged: "there's a general view that the interest rates may go up. We have not seen it happening until the month of July."
- **Pass-through policy in a volatile rate environment:** "volatility, we do not generally pass it on to customers. We also wait for it to be permanent and it should hit our balance sheet. Once the higher interest rates hits our numbers, then only we will pass it on to the customers because we have a very robust RPLR model… Any 1-month or 2-month impacts… we generally do not pass it on."
- **Opex:** cost-to-income 36.3% including ~INR 15 cr/quarter ESOP; ex-ESOP 33–34%. "if you look at it over the last 2 years, we would have dropped about **150 bps on cost to income**." Non-employee cost ambition: "if we manage to do anything like 10%, 11% growth in the full year on nonemployee cost, I think we would have done a very good job." Sequential employee-cost rise = "the annual increment, which is typically in the range of approximately 10% to 12%."
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** First note on AADHARHFC. AUM INR 31,364 cr (+18% YoY); disbursement INR 2,036 cr on the NEW cheque-clearance basis vs INR 2,359 cr like-to-like (+19% YoY); PAT INR 282 cr (+19%); spread 5.8%; GNPA 1.31%; ROA 4% / ROE 14.7%; Tier 1 42.9%. FY27 guidance reaffirmed at 20% AUM / 20% PAT / 17–18% disbursement, with Q2 disbursement growth guided "close to 25% or upward of 23%, 24%" and July 2026 disbursement stated as "very close to INR900 crores." Only 2 branches added vs a 45–50 FY27 target. No capital return planned.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did Q2 disbursement growth land at 23–25% and absorb the Q1 carry-forward; (b) branch adds against the 45–50 run-rate; (c) spread vs the ≥5.5% floor if cost of funds turns; (d) GNPA path toward the 1.1% FY-end commitment and credit cost toward 23–25 bps; (e) non-home incremental mix moving back toward 70-30 (Q3 target); (f) any change of stance on capital return._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Medium-term / FY27 headline (reaffirmed twice, opening + closing):** "we are firm and stick with our medium-term guidance of **20% AUM growth, 20% profit growth, 17% to 18% disbursement growth** for the full year."
- **Disbursement, next 3 quarters:** "Next 3 quarters, we have targeted disbursement growth of **upward of 20%**." Closing remarks: "next 3 quarter disbursement growth in excess of 20% and profit growth of 20%."
- **Q2 FY27 specifically:** "quarter 2 numbers should be there and no reason why I should have a disbelief around it, should be **close to 25% or upward of 23%, 24%**"; and "quarter 2 will substantially cover up for the short fall of quarter 1."
- **July 2026 run-rate (stated on the call):** "as I look at July, we are already at the last day of July, and we should be hitting a number **very close to INR900 crores**."
- **Spread:** "we will be a company which will be as a company with a spread of **5.5% upward**" — currently 5.8%. Over a 2–3 year period "we would be ending in the range of about 5.5%. There's no appetite to go below that."
- **Asset quality:** "we are quite confident of pulling it back to **1.1% level** as we end the fiscal and with the credit cost charge to about **23 bps to 25 bps** on the P&L."
- **Cost:** "we still have the ability to drop cost to income by approximately **30 bps to 40 bps** on a yearly basis. On a cost to AUM basis… about **6 bps to 7 bps** every year."
- **Non-home mix normalisation:** incremental home:non-home to return to **70-30** (currently "about 76-24"); "from a quarter 3 perspective, it should be back to normalcy."
- **Branch network:** "we stand by our numbers of **45 to 50 branches**" for the year (Q2 and Q3 weighted; Q4 avoided by policy).
- **Return profile, 2 years out:** steady-state ROA "anywhere between **4.3% and 4.4%**"; "ROEs… a couple of years down the line, we would be hitting around **17% ROE**."
- **Capital:** "there's no current plan of handing it back to shareholders as of now."
- **Cost of funds, near-term view:** "we don't see any imminent impacts happening in the current quarter and probably even the next quarter" — with the caveat "things may change."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- The Q1 "shortfall" is a **timing carry-forward, not lost business**: "the numbers that I have not done cheque realization moves to quarter 2." Management refused to call it a loss — "the entire business that is getting carry forward, it generally happens over a couple of quarters."
- **July 2026 disbursement tracking to ~INR 900 crores** (stated on 31-Jul, i.e. essentially the month's actual).
- Demand backdrop: "demand for low-income housing finance continues to remain healthy and structurally supported… largely end user base and first-time homebuyer driven, particularly in the emerging markets… which gives us comfort that this growth is not speculative in nature."
- **Urban demand running ahead of plan:** "the urban demand is slightly more than what we had expected at least in the last 2 quarters." No demand-side issue flagged in Tier 1/2: "No, not at all. Not that we are seeing any."
- Distribution engine: 628 branches / 22 states / 550+ districts; new branches "reach productivity level within our expected **9 to 15 months** window."
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline (disbursement pipeline / growth drivers)

outlook.body:
- **AI as an operating layer (the most differentiated disclosure on this call):** "We are institutionalizing AI as Aadhar's operating backbone — a **6-layer AI architecture** embedded across origination, underwriting, surveillance, collection and retention with every engine tiered to track outcome like NPA, turnaround time, cost to income, retention and yield. Further, we are building **5 proprietary reusable platforms** spanning across document intelligence, voice intelligence, decisioning intelligence and enterprise access layer and management intelligence that we believe compound into a genuine competitive advantage over a period of time." CFO ties it to cost: "if some of the AI projects that we are taking up… starts pushing in and improves productivity… probably we would see some more cost benefits in terms of cost to assets."
- **Emerging-market branch build-out** as the yield-defence engine (450+ of 628 branches; 45–50 more this year).
- **Non-home loan re-acceleration** back toward 70-30 incremental once the West Asia situation stabilises (targeted Q3).
- **Repricing optionality:** "75% of our assets can be repriced" via the RPLR model (ALCO + Board approval) — an explicit hedge if bank MCLRs rise.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A deliberately "quiet" quarter whose headline disbursement is depressed by an **accounting-recognition change, and management said there is "no current plan of handing it back to shareholders."
